headline: Pilbara Minerals hammered 8% as lithium selloff deepens — while oil surges past $103 on Middle East escalation fears.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS copped its biggest single-day hit in recent memory, dropping 8% to $2.62 today. Lithium prices remain under serious pressure globally — analysts are flagging key support levels are at risk, and there's no near-term catalyst to reverse the trend. The broader lithium miner selloff is the driver here, not anything company-specific.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped nearly 2% in last night's US session. No specific news out — this looks like broad tech/consumer discretionary weakness dragging it down alongside a slightly softer NASDAQ. The long-term GTA VI thesis is unchanged.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF dipped 1.35% today, tracking weakness in US tech names like Alphabet overnight. With GOOG down and AI spending scrutiny growing, the ETF felt some pressure. No structural change to the AI growth story.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE fell just over 1% today, reflecting ongoing caution around emerging markets as the Middle East situation rattles global risk appetite and oil prices surge — which can hurt energy-importing emerging economies.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet dropped 1.08% last night despite reporting strong cloud revenue growth of 82%. Investors are nervous about how much Google is spending on AI infrastructure versus what they're getting back — the market wants to see the payback pace accelerate. Q3 earnings are the key event to watch.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: DHHF barely moved, slipping 0.39% in today's session. Just gentle broad-market softness, nothing to read into here.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS eased 0.47% today, reflecting last night's mild S&P 500 pullback of 0.52%. US markets dipped slightly but nothing alarming — this is just normal market breathing.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was almost perfectly flat today, down just 0.13%. Its diversified mix of assets absorbed the day's mild volatility well.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was the standout last night, rising 0.66% against a soft market. Investors are positioning ahead of its Q3 earnings on October 28, with expectations high for Azure cloud growth and AI momentum updates. The market is clearly backing Microsoft's AI story right now.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals: Steep 8% fall — when does the bleeding stop?
watch_today.detail: PLS closed at $2.62 today, down 8% in a single session and now sitting 61% below your average buy price. The lithium market is in a genuine structural downturn — prices are weak globally, support levels are under threat, and there's no near-term catalyst. For a long-term holder, the question is whether you believe in a lithium recovery over the next 3-5 years. The investment thesis is tested but not dead — sit tight unless your conviction has changed.

watch_today.title: GOOG earnings this week — big moment for your Alphabet holding
watch_today.detail: Alphabet's Q3 results are due imminently. Last night's 1% dip came despite cloud revenue jumping 82%, with investors focused on whether AI spending is paying off fast enough. The result could move the stock sharply in either direction. For a long-term holder, the cloud and AI fundamentals look solid — but expect volatility around the print. Hold and watch.

watch_today.title: MSFT earnings on 28 October — Azure and AI in the spotlight
watch_today.detail: Microsoft reports earnings on Tuesday 28 October (US time, so early Wednesday AEST). The market is watching Azure's growth rate and whether $50B+ in capital expenditure on AI is translating to revenue. Last night's 0.66% rise suggests investors are optimistic. This is the biggest near-term catalyst for your MSFT holding — which is already up 18% overall. Hold and let the earnings play out.

watch_today.title: Oil surging past $103 — watch the flow-on effects
watch_today.detail: Crude oil jumped nearly 4% last night to $103.27 a barrel as fears of a fresh Israeli-US strike on Iran rattled energy markets. This is significant — higher oil prices feed into inflation, which could delay interest rate cuts by central banks. It also puts pressure on emerging markets (your VGE holds countries that import oil). Keep an eye on whether this escalates further.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Down 15% overall — but the AI story is still early innings
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF is sitting 14.86% below what you paid for it. Today's 1.35% dip is mostly Alphabet drag. The global AI buildout is real and ongoing — US tech leaders are actually calling for more AI rules, which signals the technology is becoming mainstream infrastructure. For a long-term holder, this is a position to sit with, not sell.

watch_today.title: Middle East tensions driving gold and oil — broad market risk to watch
watch_today.detail: Gold fell 1.3% last night to just over $4,000/oz (some profit-taking after a big run), while oil surged. The Middle East situation is live and fluid — any escalation involving Iran could spike energy prices further and spook global equity markets. Your diversified ETFs (VDHG, VTS, DHHF) give you natural protection across asset classes here.

world.summary: The Middle East is on edge with fears of a fresh US-Israeli strike on Iran, oil has surged above $103 a barrel, and US domestic politics are heating up as Democrats plan their post-Trump comeback while the administration fights Senate election results in Alaska.

stories.title: Middle East braces for fresh US-Israeli strike on Iran — oil spikes
stories.why_it_matters: Multiple countries and international bodies are warning the US and Israel not to launch new strikes on Iran, with analysts saying 'escalation is coming.' Trump has referenced another potential 'Epic Fury' operation, echoing language from previous strikes. The threat of a broader regional conflict is real — it's already pushed oil up nearly 4% to $103 a barrel overnight, which flows through to higher petrol prices and inflation for everyday Australians. Saudi Arabia has also postponed a major UN forum until 2027, citing regional tensions.

stories.title: Trump administration sues to block Alaska Senate result if Democrat Mary Peltola wins
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has pre-emptively filed a lawsuit to block the certification of the Alaska US Senate election result if Democrat Mary Peltola wins. The administration is challenging Alaska's ranked-choice voting system, which Peltola used to win her House seat. This is an extraordinary step — a sitting government trying to invalidate a state election result before it's even happened. It raises serious questions about the integrity of the US democratic process.

stories.title: Democrats crafting a plan to dismantle Trump's agenda ahead of 2028
stories.why_it_matters: US Democrats are already building a detailed policy blueprint to reverse Trump's key agenda items if they return to power — covering tariffs, immigration, climate and government spending cuts. The NYT reports the plan is more coordinated than their 2020 effort. For investors, this is a long-range signal: whoever wins in 2028 will face pressure to undo significant structural changes to the US economy, which creates policy uncertainty for years ahead.

stories.title: Latin America's MAGA wave is expanding Trump's reach across the region
stories.why_it_matters: A wave of Trump-aligned right-wing governments is taking hold across Latin America, giving the US administration growing political and military influence in the region. The Washington Post reports this trend is widening Trump's ability to project power and push his agenda internationally, with implications for trade, migration policy, and regional security alliances. For Australia, a more politically aligned Western hemisphere could shift global diplomatic dynamics.

stories.title: IMF raises 2026 growth forecast but warns stock investors of overvaluation risk
stories.why_it_matters: The IMF (International Monetary Fund — the global economic referee) has upgraded its 2026 world growth forecast, which sounds positive. But buried in the report is a warning that equity markets, particularly in the US, look overvalued relative to economic fundamentals. For long-term investors with exposure to US stocks (like VTS, VDHG and MSFT), it's a reminder that short-term corrections are possible even in a healthy economy.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 was basically flat today, up just 2 points. Last night's US session was mildly negative — S&P 500 dropped 0.52%, NASDAQ eased 0.21%. The big story is oil jumping nearly 4% on Middle East fears, while gold pulled back 1.3%. The Aussie dollar nudged up slightly to 70.38 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Essentially flat today — the local market shrugged off overnight US weakness.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session saw mild selling — nothing dramatic, just cautious trading ahead of big earnings.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech held up relatively well last night despite Alphabet's post-earnings wobble.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Big move — oil jumped nearly 4% on fears of a new US-Israeli strike on Iran. Watch this space.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold eased back 1.3% after a strong run — some profit-taking at elevated levels.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar ticked up slightly — still comfortable above 70 US cents.

politics.summary: No Australian political news made it into today's feed — a quiet Saturday on the domestic politics front. Keep an eye on the upcoming RBA meeting and any government response to rising oil prices feeding into inflation.

stories.title: No Australian political stories available today
stories.why_it_matters: The news feed didn't surface any Australian domestic political stories today. This is likely a quiet weekend news cycle. Check back Monday for any developments around the federal budget, RBA policy, or energy cost pressures from the oil price spike.

ai.summary: The big AI debate this week is about regulation — US tech leaders are calling for rules, China already has them, and Australia is worried about AI in classrooms. Meanwhile, ChatGPT still dominates the chatbot market with over half of all AI assistant usage.

stories.title: US tech giants call for AI regulation — while China already has it
stories.why_it_matters: The heads of major US tech companies — the same people building AI — are now urgently asking governments to set rules for the technology. This is a notable shift: the industry used to resist regulation. Meanwhile, China already has a formal AI regulatory framework in place. For investors in AI stocks and ETFs, regulation could be a headwind (compliance costs) or a tailwind (it legitimises the industry and reduces the 'wild west' risk that spooks institutional money).

stories.title: ChatGPT holds 56.4% of AI assistant market — Gemini and Claude trail
stories.why_it_matters: A new 2026 market share breakdown shows ChatGPT (OpenAI) controls 56.4% of the AI chatbot market, with Google's Gemini, Anthropic's Claude, and Elon Musk's Grok all fighting for the remaining scraps. For your GOOG holding, this matters — Gemini is Google's main consumer AI product, and it's still well behind ChatGPT. Google's strength remains in search, cloud, and infrastructure rather than the chatbot race.

stories.title: 'A reckoning is coming' — Australians worried about AI in classrooms
stories.why_it_matters: A new Nine/survey finds most Australians are deeply concerned about AI being used in schools — from cheating to teachers being replaced to data privacy for kids. Educators and parents are calling for clearer national rules on how AI tools can be used in classrooms. It's a real community flashpoint, and one the federal government will likely need to address in the next education policy cycle.

stories.title: Wall Street's regulator to scrutinise AI use in corporate compliance exams
stories.why_it_matters: The SEC (America's main sharemarket cop) has announced it will focus its 2027 examination program on how financial firms are using AI — specifically looking at whether AI tools are creating new risks in trading, advice, and compliance. For companies like Microsoft (which sells AI tools to banks and financial institutions), this could mean more compliance overhead for their biggest clients. It's a sign AI is moving from hype to regulation territory fast.

sport.summary: The Rugby League World Cup is in full swing — Tonga and Samoa both won big, England kept their finals hopes alive, and the women's competition is heating up. In AFL, the game is mourning the sudden death of former Port Adelaide player Daniel Stewart at age 37. Djokovic is back to his best, and the WSL surfing tour heads to the Philippines.

stories.title: Tonga smash Lebanon, set up massive Samoa showdown
stories.why_it_matters: Tonga put in a dominant display against Lebanon at the Rugby League World Cup, setting up what shapes as a blockbuster Pacific showdown against Samoa. With Samoa also winning convincingly (see below), the Pacific island nations are looking like genuine title contenders in this tournament.

stories.title: Samoa demolish PNG — Leniu the standout
stories.why_it_matters: Samoa ran over PNG in convincing fashion at the World Cup, with prop Royce Leniu putting in a starring performance. Samoa's depth of NRL talent is on full display, and they now face Tonga in what could be the match of the tournament's group stage. PNG were competitive but ultimately outclassed.

stories.title: England hammer France in World Cup — finals still on
stories.why_it_matters: England put on a 'staggering barrage' to beat an 'embarrassing' French side and keep their semi-final hopes alive at the World Cup. France's performance was described as embarrassing by Fox Sports — a poor showing from a European rival. England now needs results to go their way but remain in the hunt.

stories.title: AFL mourns sudden death of former Port Adelaide player Daniel Stewart, 37
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL community is in shock following the sudden death of former Port Adelaide player Daniel Stewart, aged just 37. No cause of death has been publicly confirmed. Stewart played for Port Adelaide and the AFL world has responded with an outpouring of grief. It's a sobering reminder of life beyond the game and has hit the football community hard.

stories.title: Djokovic wins in Beijing — best wins of a tough 2026 season ranked
stories.why_it_matters: Novak Djokovic has claimed victory in Beijing, adding another title to what's been described as a 'difficult 2026' season. Despite earlier reports he considered skipping Wimbledon after a shocking defeat, Djokovic has rallied strongly in the Asian swing. At 39, the GOAT debate continues — he's still winning at the highest level even in a challenging year.
